statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-4438 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0006, glibc bug 34015): in the GNU C Library 2.34 to 2.43, when nsswitch.conf uses the DNS backend, getanswer_ptr did not check the hostname extracted from a DNS response, so gethostbyaddr and gethostbyaddr_r could return an invalid hostname, including shell metacharacters, to an application that then uses it unguarded in a shell. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0006. Upstream fixed it on the 2.41 branch in https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=commit;h=502861645bb1baf650d58e2ddd6b230bc26676c9 (resolv: Check hostname for validity). Debian fixed it for trixie in 2.41-12+deb13u3 (Debian bug 1131887, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4438). The one glibc build published in the DHI Debian repository is Debian's 2.41-12+deb13u4 rebuilt for DHI, on amd64 and arm64; the version banner in its libc.so.6 names that Debian release (glibc 2.41). We checked the libc6 package of that build for both architectures against the repository index checksum: the Debian changelog it ships carries the 2.41-12+deb13u3 entry that applies the upstream stable-branch fix for CVE-2026-4438. The range ends at that build.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-4438 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0006) is in the DNS backend of the GNU C Library (glibc), versions 2.34 to 2.43: a defect in getanswer_ptr lets gethostbyaddr and gethostbyaddr_r accept and return an invalid DNS hostname, which can contain shell metacharacters. Debian fixed it in trixie in glibc 2.41-12+deb13u3. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0006, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4438. This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked every binary package published from the ncurses source in the DHI Debian repository for amd64 and arm64 (56 index entries in 50 distinct files, because the architecture-independent ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc are listed for both): both published rebuilds of Debian's ncurses 6.5+20250216-2 (libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, libncurses-dev, ncurses-bin, ncurses-base, ncurses-term, ncurses-doc and ncurses-examples, and the debug-symbol packages for libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, ncurses-bin and ncurses-examples). None of them contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a, libpthread or another glibc library, a glibc gconv module, the glibc version banner, a statically linked program, a PE or Mach-O file, or a jar, whl, zip or nupkg archive. The shared libraries (libtinfo, libtic, libncurses, libncursesw, libform, libformw, libmenu, libmenuw, libpanel and libpanelw) and the programs in ncurses-bin (clear, infocmp, tabs, tic, toe, tput and tset) and ncurses-examples are dynamically linked ELF files that list the system libc.so.6 in NEEDED, and the programs name the system dynamic loader (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 or ld-linux-aarch64.so.1) as their interpreter. libncurses-dev ships twelve static archives (libncurses.a, libncursesw.a, libtinfo.a, libtic.a, libform.a, libformw.a, libmenu.a, libmenuw.a, libpanel.a, libpanelw.a, libncurses++.a and libncurses++w.a, plus libcurses.a and libtermcap.a as symlinks to two of them) whose members are ncurses's own object files; a program that links them statically takes its C library from its own build, not from this package. The debug-symbol packages hold detached debug information, and ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc hold terminfo entries, tab-set files and documentation with no ELF files or archives. glibc reaches an image through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner and is assessed on its own.
